prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Membrane bioreactors with ultrafiltration can be operated continuously with enzyme recycling, achieving protein retention of 87–92% over extended periods when membrane fouling is actively managed through daily backwash protocols.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03519","field":"abstract","quote":"Enzyme retention was 87–92% across 14 days of continuous operation"}]},{"text":"Polyethersulphone ultrafiltration membranes fouled with biological process streams can recover 93–97% of pure water flux through alkaline cleaning protocols, though aggressive hypochlorite cleaning reduces membrane lifetime by approximately 18% after 30 cycles.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03378","field":"abstract","quote":"Protocol C preserved membrane integrity better and achieved PWFR of 93.1%"}]},{"text":"High-solids enzymatic hydrolysis involves complex interactions between slurry rheology, substrate properties, and enzyme kinetics that affect reactor performance and downstream separation requirements.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03514","field":"abstract","quote":"slurry rheology evolves from a shear-thinning paste to a less viscous suspension as hydrolysis proceeds"}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher has direct experience with ultrafiltration fouling in enzymatic bioprocesses and membrane cleaning protocols [SYN-PUB-03519, SYN-PUB-03378], but the published work addresses enzyme recovery systems rather than pre-filtration design or cell debris removal upstream of UF, which is the core challenge."}
